newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-UK retail sales growth to slow in Dec.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-UK retail sales growth to slow in Dec.

text.p: Annual growth in UK retail sales is expected to have slowed slightly in December, thanks to patchy and disappointing pre-Christmas spending, economists said on Monday.
But the underlying trend in consumption remains buoyant and domestic demand still looks set to be the engine of growth in 1997. December figures will be released on Wednesday.

"Both anecdotal and survey evidence suggest that retail sales in December were patchy, with a weak build-up to Christmas somewhat offset by hectic trading immediately before the holiday," said Deutsche Morgan Grenfell economist Ciaran Barr.

According to a Reuter poll, economists expect retail sales to rise by 0.1 percent in December, down from November's heady 0.7 percent jump. Annual growth is seen slowing to 3.5 percent in December from 3.9 percent the previous month.
The British Retail Consortium's December survey released last week and the CBI distributive trades survey both painted a picture of disappointing sales in the first half of December.
The BRC said retail sales growth continued to slow last month, picking up pace only a few days before Christmas.

The CBI said retail sales volumes in December were up on the December 1995 but growth was below expectations. A positive balance of 33 percent of retail firms reported higher sales year-on-year, down from 48 percent in November.
Schroders economist David Philpotts said he expected sales to fall 0.1 percent in December, giving a 3.4 percent annual growth rate.
"Our forecast envisages a modest monthly decline in retail sales in December after what was a very strong November, but a more significant contraction in expenditure is quite possible," he said.
"Even so, it would still be far too early to become gloomy about consumer spending in 1997," he added. "A modest loss of momentum does, however, suggest that talk of a boom has been overdone."
Barr agreed it was too early to talk of a slowdown in consumption. "Despite this blip, we believe the underlying trend remains buoyant, as reflected in a healthy start to the January sales," he said.

Societe Generale gilts analyst Tom Rayner said windfall gains from the conversion of some building societies into banks and a steady improvement in consumer confidence as unemployment continues to fall would ensure consumer demand growth would accelerate over 1997 as a whole.

"Moreover, it is often the case that the services part of consumer demand is strong when retail sales are weak. In other words, the softer retail sales growth does not necessarily mean softer overall consumer demand growth," he said.
